title: Make night light temperatures configurable in shell.json
author: satchlj
body:
## What

Night light was hard-coded to 4000K (on) / 6500K (off) in two places: the shell's nightlight service (`shell/plugins/services/nightlight/Service.qml`) and `bin/omarchy-toggle-nightlight`. This adds `nightlight.night` and `nightlight.day` to `shell.json` and reads them from both, so the shell indicator, the IPC toggle, the keybinding and the menu all agree.

```json
"nightlight": { "night": 4000, "day": 6500 }
```

Defaults are unchanged, so existing installs behave exactly as before.

## Why

Some of us never want a fully blue screen and use a warm baseline all day (for example day 4000K, night 2700K). Today the only way is to hand-edit two package files, which updates overwrite. Being able to set these in `shell.json`, next to the idle timeouts, is the natural place.

## Semantics

"Enabled" now means warmer than both the 6000K identity point *and* the configured day temperature. With the defaults this is identical to the current behaviour (6000 and 6500 both read as off). With a warm day baseline like 4000K, 4000K reads as off and 2700K as on, so the bar indicator and toggle still make sense.

Invalid values (non-integer, outside 1000..20000) or an inverted pair (`night >= day`) fall back to the defaults, so a typo in `shell.json` can't leave the toggle stuck.

`bin/omarchy-toggle-nightlight` resolves the config the same way `shell.qml` does: the user's `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json` when it carries `version: 1`, else `$OMARCHY_PATH/config/omarchy/shell.json`.

## Changes

- `shell/plugins/services/nightlight/NightlightModel.js`: `temperaturesFromConfig()` with validation; `isNightlight(temperature, dayTemperature)`.
- `shell/plugins/services/nightlight/Service.qml`: read `shell.shellConfig.nightlight`.
- `bin/omarchy-toggle-nightlight`: same keys via `jq`; toggle decision uses the same threshold.
- `config/omarchy/shell.json` and the built-in fallback in `shell/shell.qml`: new defaults block.
- `docs/omarchy-shell.md`: documented under the `shell.json` rules.
- `test/shell.d/nightlight-test.sh`: model cases for config resolution and the new threshold; CLI cases with a custom `shell.json` (2700/4000) and an inverted pair.

## Testing

`test/shell.d/nightlight-test.sh` passes (22 assertions). `./test/shell` on this branch shows the same failure set as untouched `quattro` on the same machine (macOS host without `magick`, bluetoothctl, etc.); no new failures.

Verified on a MacBook Neo running Omarchy 4.0.1 with `"nightlight": {"night": 2700, "day": 4000}` in `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json`: `omarchy-toggle-nightlight --status` reports 4000K as disabled and 2700K as enabled, the CLI toggle, `omarchy-shell nightlight toggle/enable`, and the stock Super+Ctrl+N binding all move between 2700K and 4000K, and the shell's status matches after each.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

files.patch:
@@ -4,9 +4,43 @@
 # omarchy:args=[--status]
 # omarchy:examples=omarchy toggle nightlight
 
-ON_TEMP=4000
-OFF_TEMP=6500
 IDENTITY_TEMP=6000
+DEFAULT_ON_TEMP=4000
+DEFAULT_OFF_TEMP=6500
+
+# Temperatures live in shell.json (`nightlight.night` / `nightlight.day`), the
+# same keys the shell's nightlight service reads. The user file replaces the
+# defaults wholesale when it carries version 1, mirroring shell.qml.
+shell_config_file() {
+  local user="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/omarchy/shell.json"
+  if [[ -f $user ]] && jq -e '.version == 1' "$user" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    printf '%s\n' "$user"
+  elif [[ -n ${OMARCHY_PATH:-} && -f $OMARCHY_PATH/config/omarchy/shell.json ]]; then
+    printf '%s\n' "$OMARCHY_PATH/config/omarchy/shell.json"
+  fi
+}
+
+configured_temp() {
+  local key=$1 fallback=$2 file value
+  file=$(shell_config_file)
+  [[ -n $file ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$fallback"; return; }
+  value=$(jq -r --arg key "$key" '.nightlight[$key] // empty' "$file" 2>/dev/null)
+  if [[ $value =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( value >= 1000 && value <= 20000 )); then
+    printf '%s\n' "$value"
+  else
+    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
+  fi
+}
+
+ON_TEMP=$(configured_temp night "$DEFAULT_ON_TEMP")
+OFF_TEMP=$(configured_temp day "$DEFAULT_OFF_TEMP")
+if (( ON_TEMP >= OFF_TEMP )); then
+  ON_TEMP=$DEFAULT_ON_TEMP
+  OFF_TEMP=$DEFAULT_OFF_TEMP
+fi
+# Night light counts as on below both the identity point and the day
+# temperature, so a warm day baseline still reads as "off".
+ENABLED_BELOW=$(( OFF_TEMP < IDENTITY_TEMP ? OFF_TEMP : IDENTITY_TEMP ))
 
 current_temp() {
   local output
@@ -19,7 +53,7 @@ status_json() {
   local temp enabled
 
   temp=$(current_temp)
-  if [[ -n $temp ]] && (( temp < IDENTITY_TEMP )); then
+  if [[ -n $temp ]] && (( temp < ENABLED_BELOW )); then
     enabled=true
   else
     enabled=false
@@ -42,7 +76,7 @@ fi
 # Query the current temperature
 CURRENT_TEMP=$(current_temp)
 
-if [[ -z $CURRENT_TEMP || $CURRENT_TEMP == $OFF_TEMP ]]; then
+if [[ -z $CURRENT_TEMP ]] || (( CURRENT_TEMP >= ENABLED_BELOW )); then
   TARGET_TEMP=$ON_TEMP
 else
   TARGET_TEMP=$OFF_TEMP

+  readonly property var nightlightConfig: shell && shell.shellConfig && shell.shellConfig.nightlight ? shell.shellConfig.nightlight : ({})

-  readonly property bool enabled: stateLoaded && NightlightModel.isNightlight(temperature)

   property bool hasPendingTemperature: false
   property int pendingTemperature: 0

@@ -13,6 +13,15 @@ assertEqual(nightlight.isNightlight(4000), true, 'nightlight reports warm temper
 assertEqual(nightlight.isNightlight(5999), true, 'nightlight reports warmer-than-identity values as enabled')
 assertEqual(nightlight.isNightlight(6000), false, 'nightlight reports identity temperature as disabled')
 assertEqual(nightlight.isNightlight(null), false, 'nightlight reports unknown temperature as disabled')
+assertEqual(nightlight.temperaturesFromConfig(undefined).night, 4000, 'nightlight defaults night temperature without config')
+assertEqual(nightlight.temperaturesFromConfig(undefined).day, 6500, 'nightlight defaults day temperature without config')
+assertEqual(nightlight.temperaturesFromConfig({ night: 2700, day: 4000 }).night, 2700, 'nightlight reads night temperature from config')
+assertEqual(nightlight.temperaturesFromConfig({ night: 2700, day: 4000 }).day, 4000, 'nightlight reads day temperature from config')
+assertEqual(nightlight.temperaturesFromConfig({ night: 'warm', day: 4000 }).night, 4000, 'nightlight ignores a non-numeric night temperature')
+assertEqual(nightlight.temperaturesFromConfig({ night: 5000, day: 4000 }).day, 6500, 'nightlight falls back when night is not below day')
+assertEqual(nightlight.isNightlight(4000, 4000), false, 'nightlight reports the configured day temperature as disabled')
+assertEqual(nightlight.isNightlight(2700, 4000), true, 'nightlight reports below-day temperatures as enabled')
+assertEqual(nightlight.isNightlight(6000, 6500), false, 'nightlight keeps identity disabled with a default day temperature')

@@ -53,6 +62,8 @@ nightlight_cli() {

@@ -90,3 +101,29 @@ if rg -q 'omarchy.indicators' "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-toggle-nightlight"; then
   fail "nightlight toggle leaves indicator refresh to the nightlight service"
 fi
 pass "nightlight toggle leaves indicator refresh to the nightlight service"
+
+# Custom temperatures from shell.json: a warm day baseline that still toggles.
+mkdir -p "$TMPDIR/config/omarchy"
+jq '.nightlight = { night: 2700, day: 4000 }' "$ROOT/config/omarchy/shell.json" >"$TMPDIR/config/omarchy/shell.json"
+
+[[ $(nightlight_status 4000 | jq -r .enabled) == "false" ]] || fail "nightlight status reports the configured day temperature as disabled"
+pass "nightlight status reports the configured day temperature as disabled"
+
+[[ $(nightlight_status 2700 | jq -r .enabled) == "true" ]] || fail "nightlight status reports the configured night temperature as enabled"
+pass "nightlight status reports the configured night temperature as enabled"
+
+printf '4000\n' >"$STATE"
+nightlight_cli >/dev/null
+[[ $(<"$STATE") == 2700 ]] || fail "nightlight toggle warms to the configured night temperature"
+pass "nightlight toggle warms to the configured night temperature"
+
+nightlight_cli >/dev/null
+[[ $(<"$STATE") == 4000 ]] || fail "nightlight toggle restores the configured day temperature"
+pass "nightlight toggle restores the configured day temperature"
+
+# Inverted or invalid values fall back to the defaults.
+jq '.nightlight = { night: 5000, day: 4000 }' "$ROOT/config/omarchy/shell.json" >"$TMPDIR/config/omarchy/shell.json"
+printf '6500\n' >"$STATE"
+nightlight_cli >/dev/null
+[[ $(<"$STATE") == 4000 ]] || fail "nightlight toggle ignores an inverted temperature pair"
+pass "nightlight toggle ignores an inverted temperature pair"

comments.body:
This overlaps the still-open #10430, which also shares Night Light configuration between the CLI and shell but uses `nightlight.temperature`. This PR extends the design to a configurable daytime baseline with `nightlight.night`/`nightlight.day`.

Linking the two so the intended schema and which PR supersedes the other can be settled before merging. The warm-day-baseline test here is a useful distinction to preserve.
